supersedes: V1X-HR-FIVE-ZONE-1 (CoachingCore/v1/HEART_RATE_FIVE_ZONE_V1.json, kept byte for byte as the historical values of REPMILE-COACHINGCORE-V1-FIVE-ZONE-AMENDMENT-1)
scope: The canonical operational heart-rate model: five zones as percentages of one maximum heart rate, always computable from a valid age (220 - age), personalisable (a declared maximum, custom zone limits), refined by a measured maximum when one qualifies. A reference intensity scale beside pace and effort; never a session target, gate, dose, progression input, medical evidence or safety release. The three-zone heartRateZones of RUN_CALIBRATION_EXTENSION_V1 is unchanged.
roundingRule: A zone's highest whole bpm is floor(maximum x upToPercent / 100), in integer arithmetic; the next zone starts one bpm above. Every whole bpm then lies in exactly one zone, and a whole bpm is in a zone exactly when its percentage of the maximum is above the zone's lower percentage and at most its upper one.
threeDomainsNote: The 65/81/89/97 bands do not nest in the three approved domains (80 / 87 per cent); no correspondence is imposed. The three-zone heartRateZones keeps its own reading and its own legitimate dependants.

ageEstimate.note: A population formula: an individual's true maximum commonly differs from it by 10 bpm or more, in either direction; on average it underestimates the maximum of older adults

customZones.meaning: the highest whole bpm of Z1, Z2, Z3 and Z4; Z5 is open above

LAB_MEASURED_MAXIMUM.rules: RUN_CALIBRATION_EXTENSION_V1 heartRate.measured (182 days, no declared break of 14 days or more since, not before a hold or return)

OBSERVED_MAXIMUM.rules: RUN_CALIBRATION_EXTENSION_V1 heartRate.observedMaximum (SSCTR-V1RC-DECISION-r1 Q6(b), unchanged): chest strap, a race, time trial or field test of 10 minutes or more at RPE 8 or more, within 365 days

disclosures.ZONES: Zones are fixed percentages of your maximum heart rate. They are a rough guide, not your personal thresholds. Pace and how the run feels govern your training.
disclosures.AGE_ESTIMATE: Your maximum is estimated from your age (220 minus age). Many people's true maximum differs from this by 10 beats a minute or more, and in older adults it is more often higher than the estimate. You can enter your own.
disclosures.ATHLETE_DECLARED_MAXIMUM: The maximum heart rate you entered; not checked by the app.
disclosures.LAB_MEASURED_MAXIMUM: The maximum your lab test reported, as you supplied it; not checked by the app.
disclosures.OBSERVED_MAXIMUM: From the highest heart rate your chest strap recorded in a hard effort; your true maximum may be higher.
disclosures.ATHLETE_CUSTOM: The zone limits you set. They stay as you set them until you change them.
disclosures.OPTICAL_MEASUREMENT: Wrist (optical) readings are often less accurate than a chest strap, especially when your effort changes quickly. This reading is shown as recorded.
disclosures.NEWER_RUNNER: For newer runners the same heart rate can mean a harder effort than the zone name suggests; go by feel.
disclosures.REFERENCE_CONFLICT: Your lab maximum is lower than a heart rate your chest strap recorded, so neither is used for your zones.
disclosures.CUE: If your heart rate stays in Z4 or higher on an easy run, consider slowing down. A low reading never means speed up.
disclosures.NOT_MEDICAL: Heart-rate zones are a training aid, not a medical measure. They never change your plan or clear a safety check.
disclosures.wording: Product-owned; the meaning must be kept

futureClassifier.input: a time series {sensor, source, samples:[{t: seconds from the start, bpm, artifact?}]} in time order (a HealthKit heart-rate sample series of one workout, for example)
